seasonMovement: Impossible arrival -> settlement -> orientation and territory -> navigation -> neighborhood recognition -> participation -> information and self-directed civic use -> provision and provider pressure -> usefulness -> lived belonging without mediation -> chosen household with different wants -> self-defined belonging under judgment.
seasonDramaticShift: Issues 1–8 are driven largely by collision with 2026 and the work of building an ordinary life. From Issue 9 forward, modern systems remain real pressure but stop being the default dramatic protagonist. Trial of Toil, Belonging, War Council and the finale are driven by usefulness, autonomy, chosen routines, different wants, responsibility and legal self-definition.

kinContinuity.composition: Two men and Astrid, the only woman.
kinContinuity.issues1To3: The three Kin are seen primarily together in or immediately around the Bushwick placement; they are not yet followed independently around the city.
kinContinuity.middleSeason: Their independent errands, relationships, routines and interests begin to appear individually.
kinContinuity.belonging: Issue 10 makes their independent city operation visible without fully cataloguing each person's life. Astrid is seen with her own key and neighbor familiarity, but the breadth of her day remains deliberately unexamined.
kinContinuity.warCouncil: Issue 11 confirms that each adult must answer the review for themselves. Astrid refuses rehearsal; the story does not preview the evidence the hearing will later uncover.
kinContinuity.finale: Issue 12 reveals the practical depth of Astrid's independent ordinary life and formally separates all five adults from the old Bjorn-centered intake classification.
kinContinuity.maleNames: Personal names remain unresolved and intentionally unlettered through Issues 11–12. Current production identities are First Male Kin / @vik.KinMan1 and Second Male Kin / @vik.KinMan2; this does not block production.

issues.title: Provision
issues.function: Spring provisioning exposes the difference between household seasonal responsibility and New York's distributed food system. Bjorn and Gunnar correctly begin winter planning in spring, confront limits on cultivating public land, then demonstrate practical weather competence during a fast spring storm. The issue ends with Bjorn's provider question unresolved and directed toward work.

issues.title: Trial of Toil
issues.function: Bjorn's crisis over usefulness becomes a character story about respect, consent, responsibility and meaningful contribution. The support group changes his behavior, but the revised middle tests that change through distinct situations—emergency action, shared household obligation, ordinary belonging, difficult advice, emotional witnessing and trust—rather than repeated requested-help exercises.
issues.status: structural tightening complete; active 24-page RexPrompt payload updated; scene-based dialogue/voice pass complete

issues.title: Belonging
issues.function: Carrie discovers that successful integration has changed her role: the household now has separate mornings, routes, errands, practical city knowledge and independent return paths. Garbage-night salvage and ordinary worker authority show the Vikings operating inside city systems Carrie never taught them. The issue ends with Carrie still useful but no longer required to run their lives.
issues.beatCoverage: Inserted New York interstitial — Separate Mornings / Useful Things / Everyone Comes Back
issues.status: production-ready 21-page inserted issue; page-level dialogue, continuity and cast audited

issues.title: War Council
issues.function: A Status Reconciliation Review forces five adults who share one household to distinguish home, city access, legal status, kinship, independence, intent and future choice. Belonging has already established their independent city lives; War Council asks what each person actually wants and prepares them to answer without one household doctrine.
issues.status: production-ready 24-page rebuilt script after Belonging extraction; page-level dialogue, continuity and cast audited

issues.title: Permanent Residency / Trial by Combat
issues.function: The Status Reconciliation Review exposes a genuine defect in the emergency intake record: Bjorn is still listed as the household responsible adult and the other four adults are carried derivatively, which cannot simply become five individual permanent statuses. The applicants must establish separate adult lives in the room; Carrie must correct her old casework assumption; Bjorn must surrender the last formal residue of authority before the Hearing Officer can grant five individual permanent temporal-resident statuses.

finaleState.ordeal: Issue 12 residency hearing functions as Bjorn's trial by combat through a genuine record defect: the emergency file still encodes him as the responsible adult for four other adults, and permanent status cannot issue individually until that hierarchy is tested and corrected.
finaleState.hearingPurpose: The institution must decide whether the emergency household classification still describes reality. The hearing can grant five individual permanent statuses only if the applicants establish separate adult agency and the old Bjorn-centered record is lawfully corrected.
finaleState.bjorn: Bjorn arrives in armor without weapons. His decisive act is not a speech: when the Hearing Officer explains that correcting the record removes his formal authority to answer for the others, he says, 'Then correct it.'
finaleState.carrie: Carrie admits she selected Bjorn as responsible adult during emergency intake because the system required one and he could answer enough questions. She earns the result by acknowledging that the designation became inaccurate and supporting five separate permanent findings.
finaleState.astrid: Astrid's independence is proven compactly through self-advocacy, navigation, errands, neighborhood relationships, and the distinction between mutual reliance and legal dependency. Belonging established that she has a life Carrie does not manage; the hearing reveals enough of that life to cure the legal record.
